moat_against: RV and transient revenue is discretionary and rate-sensitive; UK Park Holidays added FX and consumer exposure until its sale
Returns capped by rent sensitivity — MH residents are lower-income; outsized rent hikes invite political and regulatory backlash
Capital-intensive land bank: growth requires acquisitions/development at market prices; no proprietary cost advantage
Interest-rate exposure: REIT multiple and refinancing costs move with long rates despite the post-sale deleveraging
Measured ROIC history in fundamentals.json is thin (8.6% in 2016, 7.7% in 2017, null on the current filing basis) — no proven through-cycle ROIC well above the cost of capital in the computed outputs
moat_for: Residents own their homes but rent Sun's land; moving a manufactured home is costly, so turnover is very low and lot-rent increases stick — same-property adjusted blended occupancy 98.8% in Q2 2026
Structural supply constraint: restrictive zoning and NIMBY opposition make new manufactured-housing communities nearly impossible to entitle — the existing site base cannot be replicated at will
Affordable-housing shortage gives durable pricing power: ~5% MH rent increases delivered for 2026, same-property NOI +6.0% in Q2 2026 (MH +8.8%), 2026 NOI guidance raised to 4.5–5.3%
Scale: 455 developed properties / 156,130 sites in the US and Canada (June 30, 2026) after the Safe Harbor and Park Holidays exits made it a pure-play North American MH/RV platform
moat_justification: Real but narrow REIT moat: zoning-protected, irreplaceable MH sites plus high resident switching costs give durable ~5% rent growth and 98.8% occupancy, but returns are capped by resident affordability/politics, RV cyclicality, and no cost advantage on new capital; measured ROIC history is too thin in the filing-direct outputs (8.6%/7.7% in 2016/17, null since) to support a 7+.
name: SUN COMMUNITIES, INC
one_liner: Durable MH/RV REIT, moat 6/10 — does not clear 15% on owner's earnings at $118.08 (weighted IRR 8.4%, weighted IV@15% $54.36); clears 15% only below $54.36, and the OE/capex model prices its land bank at zero, so the D is a model-fit verdict as much as a price verdict.
sector: Real Estate / Manufactured housing & RV REIT
